maya: Copying notes from the all-hands Q&A / people ops section. Putting follow-ups here.

julie: First question: do we still require managers to collect peer feedback for promos? Some teams find it heavy for small scope promos.

erica: Yes we still require peer feedback. We try to keep it lightweight: 3-5 peers, written bullets only. For very small scope or urgent retention promos, we accept manager-curated input but comp committee will ask for more context.

derek: Clarify the difference between leveling change vs promotion. Im not sure when to request a "leveling" vs a "promotion".

erica: Good callout. Leveling is an administrative correction when someone is placed at the wrong level (e.g., hire at L5 but assessed at L4). Promotion is movement to a higher level based on performance. Leveling requests can be fast-tracked and don't require the full promotion window; promotions follow the cycle and rubric (or ad-hoc exception). We'll add this distinction to the handbook.

maya: Question: Are market comp updates automatic or do managers need to request adjustments? Were seeing market pressure in infra and ML.

erica: Market adjustments are not automatic. People Ops monitors comp and runs market refreshes periodically. Managers should flag retention risks and well review with the comp committee. Theres a prioritization ladder: retention-critical > hard-to-fill > standard refresh. We're updating the process doc this quarter.

julie: Bonus question: is there a formal appeals process for denied promos?

erica: We have an appeals path: first discuss with manager, then a review panel (3 people ops + 1 cross-functional IC) can re-evaluate within 30 days. If still denied, we provide written rationale and development steps. Will add a short explainer to the Promos FAQ.

hr-bot: Heads-up: open enrollment starts 2025-11-01. Benefits team AMA next Thursday.

maya: Thanks all. If you want 1:1 follow-up, tag me or @erica. Ill create the FAQ doc and link here when ready. :paperclip:
